title: Everyday verbs (1)
theme: common verbs for beliefs, feelings and everyday actions
goal: Recognise and use 20 high-frequency verbs and expressions for believing, hoping, remembering and everyday actions.

example.fr: Je ne te crois pas.
example.en: I don't believe you.

items.note: Present: *je crois, tu crois, il croit, nous croyons, vous croyez, ils croient*. Past participle: *cru*. *Je crois que…* also means “I think that…”.

example.fr: J'espère que tu vas bien.
example.en: I hope you're well.

example.fr: Je te jure que c'est vrai.
example.en: I swear it's true.

items.note: *Jurer* can also mean to curse. In Québec, cursing is usually *sacrer*.

example.fr: Tu te rappelles notre premier hiver à Québec ?
example.en: Do you remember our first winter in Québec City?

items.note: Double l when the ending is silent: *je me rappelle*, but *nous nous rappelons*. Same meaning as *se souvenir de*.

items.en: to feel (an emotion or a pain)

example.fr: J'ai ressenti une grande joie.
example.en: I felt great joy.

items.note: False friend: it does **not** mean “to resent”. Present: *je ressens, nous ressentons*.

example.fr: Je parie qu'il va encore être en retard.
example.en: I bet he's going to be late again.

example.fr: Asseyez-vous, je vous en prie.
example.en: Please, have a seat.

items.en: to be quiet, to stop talking

example.fr: Tais-toi, j'écoute les nouvelles !
example.en: Be quiet, I'm listening to the news!

items.note: *Tais-toi !* is blunt. *Taisez-vous !* is the plural or formal form. A softer option: *Chut !*

example.fr: Elle embrasse ses enfants avant de partir.
example.en: She kisses her children before leaving.

items.note: *Je t'embrasse* at the end of a message = love, hugs. Never use the verb *baiser* for “to kiss”: it is vulgar.

example.fr: Raj a épousé une Montréalaise.
example.en: Raj married a woman from Montréal.

example.fr: Ne jette pas ça, c'est recyclable !
example.en: Don't throw that away, it's recyclable!

items.note: Double t when the ending is silent: *je jette*, but *nous jetons*.

items.en: to sort out, to fix (a situation)

example.fr: Ne t'inquiète pas, on va arranger ça.
example.en: Don't worry, we'll sort it out.

items.en: That suits me. / That works for me.

example.fr: Mardi à dix heures ? Oui, ça m'arrange.
example.en: Tuesday at ten? Yes, that works for me.

example.fr: Le Canada a battu la Suède trois à un.
example.en: Canada beat Sweden three to one.

items.note: Present: *je bats, nous battons*. *Se battre* = to fight.

example.fr: La tempête a détruit le vieux pont.
example.en: The storm destroyed the old bridge.

example.fr: Le chien s'est échappé du jardin.
example.en: The dog got out of the yard.

example.fr: Cette chaleur me tue !
example.en: This heat is killing me!

items.note: Mostly figurative in everyday speech: *tuer le temps* (to kill time), *Ça me tue !* (That kills me!).

example.fr: Tout le monde est prêt ? Allons-y !
example.en: Is everyone ready? Let's go!

items.note: In everyday speech, *On y va !* is just as common.

items.en: to be in trouble, to have problems

example.fr: Si tu arrives encore en retard, tu vas avoir des ennuis.
example.en: If you're late again, you'll be in trouble.

items.fr: Je n'en crois pas mes yeux.

example.fr: Un orignal dans la rue ? Je n'en crois pas mes yeux !
example.en: A moose in the street? I can't believe my eyes!

blocks.title: Tips
blocks.body: [[Ressentir]] is a false friend: it means *to feel*, not *to resent*. [[Se rappeler]] and [[se souvenir de]] both mean *to remember*. [[Espérer]] and [[jeter]] change spelling: [[j'espère]], [[je jette]]. Two blunt commands: [[Tais-toi !]] and [[Assieds-toi !]]; with strangers say [[Asseyez-vous]]. Never use *baiser* as a verb for *kiss*.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud, then record yourself and compare.

lines.fr: Je te jure que c'est vrai.
Tu te rappelles notre premier hiver à Québec ?
lines.en: Do you remember our first winter in Québec City?

lines.fr: Ne jette pas ça, c'est recyclable !
lines.en: Don't throw that away, it's recyclable!

lines.fr: Mardi à dix heures ? Oui, ça m'arrange.
lines.en: Tuesday at ten? Yes, that works for me.

lines.fr: Tout le monde est prêt ? Allons-y !

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Answer without scrolling back. Getting something wrong now helps you remember it later.

blocks.prompt: Your manager proposes a meeting on Thursday and Thursday is perfect for you. What do you say?
optionFeedback: Je me tais = I'm keeping quiet.

blocks.prompt: A visitor arrives at your office. How do you politely invite her to sit down?
blocks.explain: With someone you don't know, use the vous form: [[Asseyez-vous]].
optionFeedback: That's the tu form, for friends and family.

blocks.prompt: I hope that you are well. (to a friend)
accept: J'espère que tu te portes bien.
blocks.explain: [[J'espère]] has a grave accent (è) because the ending is silent.

blocks.prompt: I don't believe you. (to a friend)
blocks.explain: [[croire]] → [[je crois]]; the object pronoun [[te]] comes before the verb.

blocks.text: Ne ___ pas ce papier, c'est important !
blocks.en: Don't throw away that paper, it's important!
blocks.explain: Double t when the ending is silent: [[je jette, tu jettes]].

blocks.text: Le chat s'est ___ par la fenêtre.
blocks.en: The cat got out through the window.

blocks.fr: Tu te rappelles notre premier hiver ?
accept: Tu te rappelles notre premier hiver?
blocks.explain: [[rappelles]] has a double p and a double l.

blocks.fr: Si tu arrives encore en retard, tu vas avoir des ennuis.
blocks.en: If you're late again, you'll be in trouble.
blocks.prompt: What is the speaker warning about?
blocks.explain: [[Avoir des ennuis]] = to be in trouble.

summary:
- Talk about beliefs and feelings: [[croire, espérer, jurer, se rappeler, ressentir]]
- Use everyday action verbs: [[s'asseoir, se taire, jeter, embrasser, épouser]]
- Say [[Ça m'arrange]], [[Allons-y !]] and [[avoir des ennuis]]
